additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by the presence of one or more delusions lasting at least one month, in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thinking, or marked negative symptoms seen in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. Overall functioning outside the sphere of the delusional belief can be relatively preserved, and behavior is not obviously bizarre apart from the implications of the delusion. The themes of delusions are often non-bizarre (e.g., persecutory, jealous, somatic, or grandiose) and are held with strong conviction despite clear contradictory evidence. Onset is typically in mid to late adulthood and may be associated with stress, social isolation, or sensory/cognitive changes, and the course can be chronic with fluctuating intensity but without the pervasive deterioration seen in schizophrenia.

patient.personality: He is a driven, detail-obsessed and intellectually curious agricultural engineer who combines competitive perfectionism with a deep commitment to environmental stewardship and hands-on creative hobbies.
patient.stressor: About a year ago, Michael’s company underwent a major reorganization following an intense season of crop losses and disputes over the adoption of new precision-agriculture technologies he was championing. He found himself caught between skeptical landowners, cost-cutting executives, and crews who viewed his data-driven methods with suspicion, leaving him feeling professionally undermined despite his expertise and long hours in the field. Already inclined to scrutinize every metric and pattern, he began to dwell on specific conflicts and workplace incidents, reinterpreting them in a way that increasingly centered on him and his projects, even as colleagues reassured him that nothing unusual was happening. Over the next nine months, his unwavering interpretations began to strain relationships with coworkers and his ability to supervise effectively, and when his spouse noticed that these rigid beliefs were starting to dominate conversations at home and interfere with family life, she urged him to seek psychiatric help at the recommendation of their family physician.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m stuck on certain ideas about what’s going on at work, and no matter what evidence people show me, I can’t shake these beliefs.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: For months now I’ve been absolutely convinced that a group of senior managers and a couple of landowners have quietly decided to sabotage my precision-ag projects—changing data inputs, steering crews to “accidentally” damage my test plots, even scheduling meetings without me—so they can discredit me and take credit for my ideas, and no matter how many times my wife or coworkers say it’s just normal workplace chaos, it’s crystal clear to me that there’s a coordinated effort aimed squarely at me.
